chunks: And the camels, We have made them for you as signs of God; there is good for you in them. So mention the name of God over them as they stand in a row. When they have fallen on their sides (slaughtered), eat of them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you so that you may be grateful.

key_terms.الْبُدُنَ: Singular: بَدَنَة; large camels used for sacrifice
key_terms.الْقَانِعَ: The contented one (who does not beg)
key_terms.صَوَافَ: Standing in a row with forefeet tied
key_terms.وَجَبَتْ: Fallen/prostrated (referring to the act of slaughter)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure and significance of sacrificing camels in Hajj according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, 'Al-Budn' specifically refers to the large camels used for Qurbani during Hajj, emphasizing the ritual's role as a 'Sha'irah' (symbol of God) that connects physical sacrifice with spiritual gratitude. The distribution to both the 'Qani' (content poor) and 'Mu'tarr' (needy beggars) highlights the comprehensive social welfare aspect of the ritual, reinforcing the believer's duty to acknowledge God's subjugation of nature for human benefit.
